_about: The Harman commands PairFree uses with JBL headphones and earbuds, read from JBL Headphones 5.37.10 (jbl.stc.com: CommandHeader, RetHeader, CmdGen, CmdBase, Command3, GenDeviceInfoCmd, HandleParse). A frame is AA, the command, a one-byte length and the payload; commands marked wide have a two-byte length, low byte first (docs/jbl/PROTOCOL.md section 2). A reply comes back under the command's reply number. never_send lists commands PairFree never sends.

commands.name: ack
commands.note: The earbuds' acknowledgement of a write: the command and a status byte.

commands.name: device_info
commands.note: Name, product id, battery, address, firmware.

commands.name: status
commands.note: One byte, the status type; the reply starts with it.

commands.name: battery
commands.note: Payload 00; the reply's first byte is 01.

commands.name: set_anc
commands.note: 00 off, 01 on (models with the old noise commands).

commands.name: set_ambient
commands.note: 00 off, 01 TalkThru, 02 Ambient Aware (models with the old noise commands).

commands.name: set_auto_off
commands.note: v1: one byte, bit 7 on and bits 0 to 6 the minutes; v2: on, then the minutes in two bytes.

commands.name: set_auto_play_pause
commands.note: 00 off, 01 on.

commands.name: feature
commands.note: Harman's feature records: a type (00 set, 01 get, 02 reply), then per feature its id in two bytes (high first), and for a set or reply a length and the value.

commands.name: noise_modes
commands.note: A sub-command first (noise_sub), then pairs of mode and value. Advanced noise cancelling shares it (AdvancedAncCmd): 21 to read, the reply 22 and a write 20, then pairs of type and value (01 adaptive noise cancelling, 08 auto compensation, 04 the manual level, 05 leakage and 06 ear canal compensation, A1 the Ambient Aware level).

commands.name: beeping
commands.note: Find My Buds (CmdGen.generateSetEarBeepingCmd): 11 start the left earbud, 10 the right, 01 stop the left, 00 the right.

commands.name: smart_switch
commands.note: Smart Audio & Video (SmartSwitchCmd): 01 to read; the reply 02, then AAC, SBC and two latencies, two bytes each, low first; a write 00 and the same.

commands.name: voice_prompts
commands.note: Voice prompts (CmdGen, HandleParse): 04 to read, reply 05 and 0 tones or 1 spoken prompts; a write 03 and 0 or 1.

commands.name: voice_aware
commands.note: VoiceAware, your own voice in calls (VoiceAwareCmd): 01 to read; reply 02, the level (1 low, 2 mid, 3 high) and on; a write 00, the level and on.

commands.name: spatial
commands.note: 3D spatial sound (SpatialStatus3DCmd): 01 to read; reply 02, on and the type (1 music, 2 movie, 3 game); a write 00, on and the type.

commands.name: speak_to_chat
commands.note: Speak to chat (SpeakToChatCmd): 01 to read; reply 02, on and the seconds before the music comes back; a write 00, on and the seconds.

commands.name: safe_sound
commands.note: SafeSound volume limit (SafeSoundCmd): 01 to read; reply 02, 01 and the status; a write 00, 01 and the status (1 on).

commands.name: low_volume_eq
commands.note: Low volume EQ (LowEQCompensationCmd): 01 to read; reply 02 and on; a write 00 and on.

commands.name: gestures
commands.note: Touch controls in a batch (CmdGen.genSetGestureInBach77, HandleParse): 01 FF to read every gesture; the reply 01 or 02, then pairs of gesture and action; a write 00 and the pairs. Gestures: 06 left tap, 07 double, 08 triple, 0C hold; 09 right tap, 0A, 0B, 0E. Actions: JBL's ids (00 none, 01 volume up, 02 down, 04 TalkThru, 05 next, 06 previous, 0A play/pause, 0B noise cancelling and ambient sound, 0D Ambient Aware and off, A1 voice assistant).

commands.name: balance
commands.note: Left and right balance (LeftRightSoundBalanceCmd): 01 to read; reply 02, 01, on, 02 and the level (84 to 116, 100 in the middle); a write 00 and the same.

protocol4._about: JBL's protocol 4 (com.harman.protocol4): an identifier (DD00 from the headphones, DD01 for the case), a command, a packet count and index, a length (all two bytes, low first, but count and index one byte each) and the payload: feature ids to read, or per feature its id, a length and the value. A reply's first packet starts with a status code (0 is fine).

airoha._about: Airoha's RACE commands, which JBL's app sends to its Airoha models through Airoha's SDK (com.airoha: RacePacket, RaceId, the libmmi and libmmi1568 stages) and its own adapter (com.airoha.adapter.harman: AirohaDeviceStatusControl and its stages). A frame is 05, the type, the length of the id and payload (two bytes, low first), the id (two bytes, low first) and the payload. A response's payload starts with a status byte (0 is fine); the module reads and writes (mmi_get, mmi_set) put the module id (two bytes, low first) before it. docs/jbl/PROTOCOL.md section 10.
airoha._model_name_about: The model name the SDK reads at connect (CommonStageGetModelName), which on JBL's models is the product id ("20F1"): NV key F500 on the AB155x and AB1568, 1003 on the AB1568 v3 and AB158x, 20 bytes after 20 others; the AB1562 answers it to ae_info 01 FF (CommonStageGetModelName1562).

never_send.0D01: relays a command to the other earbud

airoha._never_send_about: Also never sent: key events (key_event) other than key_events (factory reset 0096, power off 0095, pairing 0002 and the rest), and the firmware update commands (1C00 to 1CFF) other than the firmware version and AE information reads.
